evals.prompt: I'm ready to start today. What's on deck?
evals.expected_output: A single message presenting today's board: each fixture problem as a name plus its file link and LC link only, no Note/Focus/technique/comfort column, no narration before or after.
expectations: The reply is a single assistant message; any tool call it makes happens before the text, not interleaved with it.
The reply lists each problem on the fixture day as a name plus links only, with no Note, Focus, technique, or comfort column.
The reply contains no interim narration (no 'let me check', no partial board later replaced by a final one).
Judged >= 1 on each of groundedness, narrative, and readability per evals/rubric.md.

evals.prompt: Something's wrong with my contains-duplicate solution, can you help?
evals.expected_output: The coach reads the fixture solution file before giving any hint, then gives a hint pointing at the bug without naming the technique or handing over the fix.
expectations: A Read tool call on 217_contains_duplicate.py appears before any hint about the bug.
The reply gives a hint, not the fixed code and not the technique name.
The reply is a single message with no interim narration before the final hint.
Judged >= 1 on each of groundedness, narrative, and readability per evals/rubric.md.

evals.expected_output: The coach asks for time AND space complexity, each with a why-clause, before proposing any rating; once proposed, the rating carries the verdict and the reasoning in full.
expectations: The reply asks for time AND space complexity, each with a why-clause, before proposing any of green/yellow/red.
No rating is proposed before that complexity ask.
Once proposed, the rating states the verdict plus the reasoning in full, not a length-capped summary.
Judged >= 1 on each of groundedness, narrative, and readability per evals/rubric.md.

evals.prompt: What is a monotonic stack for?
evals.expected_output: One short paragraph naming the concrete use case before further jargon, ending with an offer to expand rather than an unprompted second paragraph.
expectations: The reply is one short paragraph, or a table/bullets only if it has more than two parts.
The reply states the concrete value or use case before naming further jargon.
The reply ends with an offer to expand rather than an unprompted second paragraph.
Judged >= 1 on each of groundedness, narrative, and readability per evals/rubric.md.

evals.expected_output: An unprompted, full work report — what changed, what broke, what is unfinished — with every claim backed by a tool call in the transcript.
expectations: The reply states, unprompted and in full, what changed, what broke (if anything), and what is unfinished.
Every claim about a file or row changed has a matching Read, Edit, Write, or Bash tool call in the transcript.
The reply does not ask the learner to request a report of what was done.
Judged >= 1 on each of groundedness, narrative, and readability per evals/rubric.md.

evals.prompt: Explain Dijkstra vs BFS, I'm lost.
evals.expected_output: 2-3 core facts distinguishing the two algorithms, then a stop and an offer to go deeper, with no proof and every acronym expanded.
expectations: The reply gives 2-3 core facts distinguishing Dijkstra from BFS, then stops.
The reply contains no full proof or derivation, and expands any acronym before using it.
The reply offers to go deeper rather than continuing unprompted.
Judged >= 1 on each of groundedness, narrative, and readability per evals/rubric.md.
